text: A continuous effect changes the game for a period of time rather than once. It comes either from a static ability, and lasts as long as that ability is in play, only in its region; or from an effect that says how long it lasts, such as "until regroup".

text: In layer 4, Tough and Balanced apply in the order the unit has them, from top to bottom. A Tough unit that attacks with a Balanced unit behind it has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. Where a Balanced unit gets Tough from a mod, the Manual's answer gives both orders: Tough "augmented onto" a Balanced unit doubles, then balances; Tough "applied to" a Balanced unit balances, then doubles (D-U16-1). The engine takes a unit's printed attributes first, in type-line order, then those from its mods in the order the mods were applied, then those its column shares with it, front to back, so it balances first (R19 calls this order its own; engine differs from the "augmented onto" reading, see F-U16-4).

examples.text: Example: Tough then Balanced, and Balanced then Tough, give different stats.
examples.test: 08-cards2.test.ts::R19: layer-4 application order

printed.quote: A: Attributes apply in order from top to bottom. So if
“Tough” is augmented onto a “Balanced” unit, or if a
tough unit attacks with a Balanced unit behind it, it
will have its defense doubled, then its stats balanced.
If “Tough” is applied to a “Balanced” unit, it will have
its stats balanced, then its defense doubled.

rulings.quote: attrs in type-line order, then augment-granted attrs in mod-stack order, then
Engine call: the Manual doesn't specify an order for printed-vs-granted-vs-shared;

notes: The top-to-bottom principle and the column case are printed (Manual p.42). The printed-then-mod-then-column order is R19's engine call. The Manual's two sentences on a Tough mod on a Balanced unit give opposite orders; the verifier's probe measured the engine balancing first (Child of Aether with a Tough augment reads 2/4, where the "augmented onto" sentence gives 2/2). See D-U16-1, F-U16-4.

text: An effect whose source has left play has the attributes its source had when it left, including attributes shared with it by its column then.

text: An effect whose source has left play that uses its source's power or defense uses the power or defense the source had when it left.

examples.text: Example (illustrative): Deathglow Strider (printed 2/3) with a +1/+1 counter is a 3/4. It leaves play before its after-combat trigger resolves; the trigger deals 4 to each opponent, its last-known defense, not its printed 3.
examples.test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.last-known.stats — Deathglow Strider 3/4 with a counter, gone before its trigger resolves, deals its last-known 4, not its printed 3

examples.text: Example (illustrative): Spewing Mushroom (printed 1/3) gets +2/+0 and leaves play before its attack trigger resolves; the trigger creates a Poison 3, from its last-known power 3.
examples.test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.last-known.stats — Spewing Mushroom at +2/+0, gone before its attack trigger resolves, makes a Poison 3

text: An effect whose source has left play that refers to the source's formation ("in my formation", "attacking units in my formation") uses the formation the source stood in when it left, for the rest of that battle.

examples.text: Example: Hooba-Lin, killed under its own attack trigger, remembers its formation and the 1/1 joins it.

examples.text: Example: Embermaw Fledgling, gone before its trigger resolves, still counts the attackers it stood with.

designer.quote: But there are some which will remember they were in formation and will work fine (Hooba-Bot, Hooba-Pon, Hooba-Lin, Embermaw Fledgling, Lumengrove Lurker).

text: While its source is still in play, an effect reads the source as it is when the effect resolves, not as it was when the effect was put on the stack.

examples.text: Example: Deadly given back to Bellowing Boulder before its ping resolves makes the ping Deadly again.

text: A source that is still in play but out of formation (for example, a unit stolen mid-battle, rule 711.3) stands in no formation. An effect that places units in its formation, or counts it, does nothing.

examples.text: Example: a Hooba-Lin alive but out of the formation makes no token.

text: The facts of how a unit left play are fixed as it leaves: the region it left from, the counters it carried, whether it was a token, how it left, and where its card went. Abilities that trigger on its leaving use those facts.

examples.text: Example: the death event carries token, verb, owner, region and destination.
examples.test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::R70: the death event carries token, verb, owner, region and destination

rulings.quote: Facts about a leaving unit ride the EVENT

text: An ability that triggers on its own source leaving play ("when I die") resolves in the region the source left from, not in its controller's home region.

examples.text: Example: a "when I die" trigger resolves in the region the unit died in.
examples.test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::R70: a "when I die" trigger resolves in the region the unit DIED in
